title: Introducing the Stem Cell ASCL2 Reporter STAR into Intestinal Organoids
protocol: Split HEK293T cells to 25%–30% confluency in T75 flask or 100 mm petri dish and plate in DMEM supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (DMEM/FBS).
Mix transfection solution thoroughly.
Incubate the transfection mixture at 20°C for 15 minutes.
Drip 127 μL of DNA transfection solution onto HEK293T cells growing in DMEM/FBS.
Store the treated cells in a humidified cell culture incubator at 37°C.
Aspirate medium from HEK293T culture plates carefully.
Add 8 mL of DMEM/FBS to each plate.
Prepare transduction medium as described in section “Additional Organoid Media Required for Lentiviral Transduction (Protocol A)”.
Pre-cool ultracentrifuge to 4°C before beginning the procedure.
If dead cells are floating in the culture medium, collect supernatant in 15 mL flask and centrifuge for 5 min at 500 × g.
Continue with supernatant.
Collect the culture medium from the plates and push it through a 0.45 μm filter using a large 60 mL syringe.
Load ultracentrifuge buckets with tubes and pipet virus suspension into the tube.
Combine culture media of up to 4 plates into one ultracentrifugation bucket.
Equal balance opposite buckets by topping up with DMEM/FBS.
Cap buckets carefully with corresponding lids.
Centrifuge for 2.5 h at 170,000 × g at 4°C.
Prepare N∗550 μL transduction medium with N being the total number of flasks or plates in which virus has been produced.
Transfer ultracentrifuge buckets carefully into a laminar flow hood.
Open bucket containing ultracentrifuge tube and decant medium carefully so that the opaque brown pellet is on the upper side of the tube.
Take a micropipette and remove leftover medium, while taking care not to agitate the pellet.
Resuspend the virus pellet in N∗500 μL of organoid transduction medium.
Use 250 μL virus suspension (N/2) to transduce organoids grown in 50–100 μL Matrigel.
Aliquot residual virus suspension in single-use fractions and freeze at -80°C.
Pre-heat water bath to 37°C.
Pre-cool centrifuge to 4°C.
Harvest organoids with ice-cold medium and transfer into a 15 mL tube.
Top up to 10 mL with ice-cold Advanced DMEM and spin at 4°C, 300 × g for 5 min.
Discard supernatant.
Optional: If residual Matrigel is visible (not a clean pellet), repeat steps involving centrifugation and discarding the supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 500 μL trypsin.
Incubate for about 3 min in a 37°C water bath until organoids have dissociated into single cells or small fragments.
Inactivate trypsin by adding 500 μL trypsin inhibitor (1:1 ratio with trypspin), top up to 10 mL with Advanced DMEM, and spin at 4°C, 500 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend pellet in 20 μL transduction medium.
Add 250 μL virus suspension to the organoids and spin at RT, 75 × g for 1 h.
Incubate samples in a 37°C incubator for 1–4 h with a loosened lid.
Spin samples at RT, 500 × g for 5 min.
Take off supernatant and resuspend cell pellet in 100–200 μL Matrigel.
Plate in 10 μL droplets onto a pre-warmed 24-well plate with 4–5 droplets per well.
Incubate plate upside-down in the incubator for 10–20 min until the Matrigel has solidified.
Add 500 μL organoid medium supplemented with 10 μM Y-27632 to each well.
Reheat water bath to 37°C.
Cool centrifuge to 4°C.
Thaw Matrigel on ice.
Mix 100 μL BTX electroporation solution with 10 μL STAR reporter DNA and 5 μL miniTol2 transposase for each electroporation condition.
Label collection tubes for post-electroporation samples.
Dilute 0.05 g Dispase II in 500 μL Advanced DMEM/F12 to prepare a 100× dispase stock.
Add 100 μL of the 100× dispase stock to 9.9 mL Advanced DMEM/F12 to prepare 1× dispase solution.
Replace organoid medium with transfection medium, using 500 μL per well in a 24-well plate.
Add 1.25% v/v DMSO to the transfection medium.
Keep organoids in the incubator for 2–4 h after adding DMSO.
Collect organoid droplets using 1× dispase and transfer into a 15 mL tube.
Incubate in 37°C water bath for 3–10 min until Matrigel is properly dissolved.
Harvest organoids with ice-cold medium and transfer into a 15 mL tube.
Top up to 10 mL with cold Advanced DMEM/F12 and spin at 4°C, 300 × g for 5 min.
If a clean organoid pellet is visible, discard the supernatant.
Carefully take off the clear supernatant on top of the Matrigel cloud (approx. 8 mL of supernatant).
Repeat steps to ensure the organoids are properly collected and washed.
Resuspend pellet in 1 ml of trypsin.
Incubate for about 3 min in a 37°C water bath until organoid have dissociated into small fragments.
Inactivate trypsin by adding 1 ml of trypsin inhibitor (1:1 ratio with trypsin).
Top up to 10 mL with Advanced DMEM/F12, and spin at 4°C, 500 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL Advanced DMEM/F12, and roughly estimate the cell number by counting.
Pellet cells again by spinning at 4°C, 500 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant and put tube on ice.
Resuspend cell pellet in 115 μL electroporation mixture and transfer 100 μL into electroporation cuvette.
Cap the cuvette with its lid and place the cuvette in the cuvette holder of the electroporator.
Measure the impedance and adjust if value outside 30–55.
Add residual cell suspension to the cuvette to increase the number of cells being electroporated, if needed.
Electroporate cells with the settings indicated.
Add 400 μL of Opti-MEM supplemented with 10 μM Y-27632 to the electroporation cuvette.
Transfer the cells from the cuvette into an Eppendorf tube using a plastic pipette and put on ice.
Rest cells for 10–20 min on ice.
Spin tubes at 4°C, 500 × g for 5 min.
Take off supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in approximately 200 μL Matrigel.
Plate cells at high density in 10 μL droplets onto a pre-warmed 24-well plate with 4–5 droplets per well.
Incubate the plate upside-down in the incubator for 10 minutes until the Matrigel has solidified.
Add 500 μL transfection medium + 1.25% DMSO per well and incubate for at least 30–60 minutes.
Refresh each well with 500 μL transfection medium without DMSO.
Replace medium with 500 μL standard culture medium on day 3.
Start the selection procedure, 3–7 days after transfection.
Prepare 1× dispase by adding 100 μL of 100× dispase stock to 9.9 mL Advanced DMEM/F12 and mix by vortexing briefly.
Replace organoid medium with 500 μl transfection medium per well on day 1.
Take off the medium from wells containing organoids on day 2.
Collect organoid droplets using 1× dispase and transfer into a 15 mL tube.
Incubate in 37°C water bath for 3-10 minutes until Matrigel is properly dissolved.
If a clean organoid pellet is visible, discard the supernatant.
Carefully take off the clear supernatant on top of the Matrigel cloud (approx. 8 mL of supernatant).
Discard supernatant and resuspend pellet in 250 μL of trypsin.
Incubate for about 3 min in a 37°C water bath until organoids have dissociated into single cells or small fragments.
Inactivate trypson by adding 250 μL of trypsin inhibitor (1:1 ratio with trypsin).
Top up to 10 mL with Advanced DMEM.
Spin at 4°C, 500 × g for 5 min.
Take off supernatant and put cells on ice.
Mix 50 μL Opti-MEM + 0.5 μL STAR reporter DNA at 1 μg/mL + 0.25 μL miniTol2 transposase at 1 μg/mL + 2.25 μL X-tremeGENE 9 in a tube.
Vortex the mixture well.
Spin the tube briefly to remove drops from the lid or side of the tube.
Incubate for 15 min at room temperature.
Resuspend cell pellet in 225 μL transfection medium previously prepared as described.
Add N*53 μL transfection mixture to the cell suspension.
Mix well by pipetting up and down.
Incubate for 5–6 h in the incubator with a loosened lid.
Thaw Matrigel on ice and keep it on ice after thawing.
Spin tubes at 4°C, 500 × g for 5 min.
Take off supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in Matrigel.
Plate cells in 10 μL droplets onto a pre-warmed 24-well plate with 4–5 droplets per well.
Incubate the plate upside-down in the incubator for 10 min until the Matrigel has solidified.
Add 500 μL transfection medium to each well.
Replace medium with 500 μL standard culture medium on day 3.
Start selection procedure, 3 days after transfection.
Refresh medium and supplement with the appropriate selection antibiotic.
Add puromycin at 1-4 μg/mL to the medium.
Add blasticidin at 2-50 μg/mL to the medium.
Conduct a dose-response test on non-transduced/transfected organoids if sensitivity varies across lines.
Keep organoids on selection medium for at least 1–2 passages.
Passage organoids to single cells during the selection process.
FACS-purify STAR+ cells and grow them into a culture if necessary.
Pick individual organoids grown from a single cell state to establish a clonal culture.
Continue to culture organoids in the absence of the selection drug.
FACS-purify STAR+ cells and grow them into a line.
Pick individual organoids grown from a single cell state to establish a clonal culture.
Monitor organoid density carefully to ensure no fusing occurs during outgrowth.
Plate cells at a density supporting single-cell outgrowth for sensitive lines.
Replate intact organoids into larger volumes over subsequent weeks as needed.
Ensure organoids exceed 300 cells in size prior to picking for successful passaging.
Grow organoids as large as possible while maintaining clonality and culturing conditions.
Pick clonal organoids at three time points: initial plating, after selection, or after FACS purification of single STAR+ cells.
Label Eppendorf collection tubes and put them on ice.
Optional: Add 10 μL of Advanced DMEM/F12 into each collection tube to more easily release the organoids into medium.
Select a Matrigel droplet with a big STAR fluorescent organoid using a table-top microscope.
Discard culture medium of the selected culture well.
Use 50 μL ice-cold (4°C) Advanced DMEM/F12 to dissolve selected Matrigel droplet by tilting the culture plate and placing a pipette-tip above the droplet.
Take up the Matrigel droplet and transfer it into a 15 mL falcon tube.
Optional: Add 200 μL 1× dispase to the tube and incubate at 37°C for 5 min until Matrigel is properly dissolved.
Top up to 10 mL with ice-cold Advanced DMEM/F12 and carefully pellet organoids by spinning at 300 × g at 4°C for 4 min.
Take off medium from the organoids.
Resuspend organoids in 100 μL Advanced DMEM/F12.
Increase volume of Advanced DMEM/F12 if many organoids are present to facilitate handling.
Spot organoid suspension onto the inside lid of a 10 cm culture dish.
Create droplets approximately 20 μL in volume for easier manipulation.
Take up the medium droplet containing one organoid and transfer the organoid into a separate collection tube by carefully pipetting up and down.
Verify that the organoid is transferred.
Carefully take up single organoids using a 20 μL pipet if multiple organoids are in the same droplet, while checking through the oculars that other organoids stay put.
Transfer organoid into an Eppendorf tube.
Keep Eppendorf tubes on ice while picking.
Add 100 μL fresh Trypsin EDTA and incubate at 37°C for 5 min, vortexing every minute.
Mechanically disrupt organoid by adding 200 μL cold Advanced DMEM and pipetting up and down with a p200 tip several times if recommended step is not suitable.
Check under the microscope that the organoids have dissociated into small fragments/single cells.
Prolong the trypsin incubation step if necessary.
Add 100 μL trypsin inhibitor and top up to 1 mL with Advanced DMEM.
Spin Eppendorf tube at 4°C, 500 × g for 5 min.
Carefully take off supernatant while leaving 5-10 μL supernatant to not agitate the pellet.
Add 30-50 μL Matrigel and mix gently by pipetting up and down.
Plate Matrigel in 2 droplets onto a pre-warmed 48-well plate with one droplet per well.
Incubate the plate upside-down in the incubator for 10–25 min until the Matrigel has solidified.
Add 250 μL of organoid medium containing 10 μM Y-27632 and 100 μg/mL primocin.
